name: What’s the difference between an ADU and a JADU?

mainEntity.name: Is a junior ADU a better choice than a full ADU for a small lot or a family caregiver space?
mainEntity.text: Is a junior ADU a better choice than a full ADU for a small lot or a family caregiver space?

acceptedAnswer.text: A junior ADU is typically the better option when a homeowner wants to add living space inside the existing house without building a full standalone unit. It is usually smaller, less expensive, and faster to design and permit than a detached ADU. That makes it useful for a caregiver suite, family member housing, or a rental-oriented conversion where privacy is less important. A full ADU, by contrast, gives more independence, better long-term value, and greater design flexibility, but it usually takes more time and budget. The right choice depends on available square footage, privacy needs, parking or access constraints, and whether the homeowner wants a temporary family solution or a separate income-producing residence. Many homeowners overlook the difference in functionality and approval complexity, so the best answer starts with how the space will actually be used.
acceptedAnswer.description: A JADU is a smaller unit created within the footprint of an existing single-family home, while a full ADU is a separate independent dwelling unit. JADUs are usually smaller, simpler, and faster, but they offer less privacy and less design flexibility.
